data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'g-h-t', meaning to help, support, or aid. In Islamic history, the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) was called Mughith (Helper) when he assisted and supported the early Muslim community.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that symbolizes the belief in God's help and support in times of need.

in_arabic.name: مغيثي
in_arabic.long_meaning: مغيثي هو اسم علم عربي يُرمي بالغيث، وهو اسم من أسماء الله الحسنى، يُشير إلى الشخص الذي يُغيث الناس بكل ما يحتاجون. يُعتبر هذا الاسم من أسماء الله التي تُشير إلى فضل الله على عباده، ويُعتبر أيضاً اسمًا من أسماء الأنجاد في القرآن الكريم. يُحتسب هذا الاسم من ضمن الأسماء التي تنمى الشخصية الإنسانية، ويُعتبر اسماً مناسبًا للشخص الذي يُريد أن يكون كريمًا ومغيثًا لأهله.

in_urdu.name: مغیثی
in_urdu.meaning: اسم مغیثی جو پر غیث کی طرف ہوتا ہے
in_urdu.long_meaning: مغیثی ایک عربي نام ہے جو پر غیث کی طرف ہوتا ہے اور یہ نام اللہ کے فضل کا نام ہے۔ یہ نام انسان کے لیے جو کرم اور فضل کرنا چاہتا ہو اس کے لیے بہت اچھا ہے۔ اس نام کے ذریعے انسان کو اللہ کے فضل اور کرم کی وجہ سے ایک غنی اور کریم بننے کی صلاحیت حاصل ہوتی ہے۔

in_hindi.name: मुगीती
in_hindi.meaning: नाम जो गर्मी के समय में वर्षा की और होता है
in_hindi.long_meaning: मुगीती एक अरबी नाम है जो गर्मी के समय में वर्षा की और होता है। यह नाम एक अच्छे इंसान के लिए उपयुक्त है जो समाज में अपनी सेवाओं के माध्यम से गरीबों की मदद करता है। यह नाम एक अच्छे इंसान के व्यक्तित्व को प्रदर्शित करता है जो दूसरों की भलाई के लिए काम करता है।

in_pashto.name: مغیثي
in_pashto.long_meaning: مغیثي د یوګذت نوموږی یو ګذت دی چې په پښتو ټولنه کې یې د ځانګړي ارزښت لري. دغه نوم د انسان سره د غیث په څیري کې د هغه د کرامت او فضل په ځاینې کې څرګندويي کوي. دغه نوم د انسان د کرم اور د غیث په څیري کې د هغه د کرامت او فضل په ځاینې کې څرګندويي کوي.

in_english.name: Mughithi
in_english.meaning: name that means 'one who brings forth blessings and favors'
in_english.long_meaning: Mughithi is a name that means 'one who brings forth blessings and favors' in Arabic. It is derived from the root word 'm-g-th', which means 'to bring forth blessings and favors'. In Islamic tradition, this name is associated with the concept of Barakah, or divine blessings, and is considered a name that brings good fortune and prosperity to its bearer. A person with this name is expected to embody the qualities of kindness, generosity, and compassion, and to be a source of comfort and support to those around him.

data.cultural_impact: The name Mughithi holds an important place in Islamic history as it refers to the prophet Muhammad (pbuh) as a helper and supporter, highlighting his role in aiding and protecting the Muslim community during its infancy. It serves as a reminder of the prophet's compassionate and selfless approach to society, emphasizing the importance of mutual support and solidarity amongst believers.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Mughithi also embodies the spiritual principle of helping one another in righteousness and piety as commanded in the Quran (Al Imran: 104). It encourages individuals to follow in the footsteps of our beloved prophet, Muhammad (pbuh), by being a source of aid and comfort for those in need, while also striving for personal and collective spiritual growth and development. The name serves as a daily reminder of the importance of helping others, both in the physical and spiritual realms.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidya wa'l-Hijra (Islamic History), Volume 9, page 138-139. Mughith Al-Din Abu Zayd (Abu Bakr) Al-Ansari was appointed as the governor of Mecca in 524 AH (1130 AD). He is known as Mughith Al-Din (the Giver of Religion). During his rule, he expelled the Banu Shayban from Mecca and brought peace to the region.
historical_references.context: Appointed as the governor of Mecca and brought peace to the region by expelling the Banu Shayban.

historical_references.reference: Tarikh Dimashq (The Book of Damascus) by Ibn Asakir, Volume 49, page 120. Mughith Al-Din Al-Kawwas was a Muslim general during the reign of Salahuddin Ayoubi (Saladin). He was killed in the Battle of Khawlan, 1179 AD. His name was given to him because he was successful in granting victory to his forces.
historical_references.context: Muslim general during the reign of Salahuddin Ayoubi and was given the name Mughith Al-Din because of his success in granting victory to his forces.
